verification.heading: Verification pass — September 25, 2026
verification.markdown:
Checked 2026-09-25 by verification agent (sweep #2). Laws cited as of Sep 2026. **Method note:** WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted) and WebFetch is robots-blocked on docs.legis.wisconsin.gov, so the official statute/code pages were read in a browser session on docs.legis.wisconsin.gov itself (HTML section pages plus the official chapter 709 PDF; text taken from the official host, no mirror). Job 1 was done by primary-host fetch, not search.
- **Job 3 item 1: disclosure form chimney/fireplace line:** RESOLVED on official host. § 709.03 form item B5: "Are you aware of defects in a woodburning stove or fireplace or of other defects caused by a fire in a stove or fireplace or elsewhere on the property?" Its examples include "defects in the chimney, fireplace flue, inserts, or other installed fireplace equipment". Item B6 covers smoke/CO detectors. § 709.02(1): 10-day delivery; 2-business-day rescission if not delivered. Sources: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/709/03 (HTML; table "See PDF") and https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/709.pdf (official PDF; published 9-4-26). Evidence class GOV.
- **Job 3 item 2: 3-day cancel:** CORRECTED and RESOLVED on official host. The old file put the 3-day cancel in ATCP 110.07. That was wrong: ATCP 110.07 is cancellation/refund for late performance. The 3-day right is Wis. Stat. § 423.202(1): "until midnight of the 3rd business day after the merchant has given the notice" under § 423.203. It applies to "consumer approval transactions" (§ 423.201: face-to-face solicitation away from the business, or directed mail/phone solicitation; credit or cash over $25). The emergency waiver is § 423.202(4). ATCP 110.08 applies ch. 423 to home improvement contracts, and ATCP 127.74(4) makes failing to give or honor the notice a prohibited face-to-face practice. Consumer Act scope cap (§ 421.202(6)): cash price over $25,000 is excluded, becoming $50,000 on 1-1-2027 under 2025 Wis. Act 105; first-lien mortgage transactions are excluded (§ 421.202(7)). Sources: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/423/II/201 ; https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/atcp/090/110/07 ; https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/atcp/090/127/IV/64 (ATCP 127.74 text on page) ; https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/421/II/202. Evidence class GOV.
- **Job 3 item 3: Dwelling Contractor scope (SPS 305):** RESOLVED on official host. SPS 305.31(1): "no person may obtain a building permit for a one- or 2-family dwelling unless" the person holds a Dwelling Contractor or Dwelling Contractor–restricted certification and holds or employs a certified DCQ. Owner-occupants are exempt (§ 101.654(1)(b)). The text has no new-construction limit, and § 101.61(1) defines "dwelling" as any building with 1 or 2 dwelling units. The only remaining interpretive point is which chimney jobs need a permit, which is local/UDC and is carried as a caveat. Sources: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/administrativecode/SPS%20305.31 ; https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/101/II/654 ; https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/101/II/61 ; https://dsps.wi.gov/Pages/Professions/DwellingContractor/Default.aspx. Evidence class GOV.
- **Bond/insurance amounts:** CORRECTED. The old file said "$25,000 bond or $250,000 liability insurance". § 101.654(2)(a) requires a bond "of not less than $5,000" or general liability insurance of "at least $250,000 per occurrence". Under § 101.654(2m), a bond under $25,000 yields a restricted certificate and caps job size at the bond amount. Source: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/101/II/654. Evidence class GOV.
- **DCQ course:** CORRECTED/partly RESOLVED. SPS 305.315 requires "at least 12 hours in an approved course in dwelling construction within one year prior to the date of application" and 12 hours CE per renewal. The earlier "+ test" is not in the rule text and has been removed. Source: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/administrativecode/SPS%20305.315. Evidence class GOV.
- **UDC scope:** RESOLVED. SPS 320.02–320.04: effective dates Dec 1, 1978 (SPS 322) and June 1, 1980 (others). Additions/alterations to UDC dwellings must comply. Municipalities may extend the code to existing dwellings or require permits outside it (SPS 320.02(2)(c)–(d)). SPS 320.08 requires a uniform building permit before on-site construction. The file's "relines/rebuilds are generally permit work" is softened to "check locally". Sources: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/administrativecode/SPS%20320.02 ; https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/administrativecode/SPS%20320.08 ; https://dsps.wi.gov/Pages/Programs/UDC/Default.aspx. Evidence class GOV.
- **CO law:** RESOLVED (official host). § 101.647(3)(a) text is as summarized; the history (2009 a. 158; 2015 a. 55; 2017 a. 330) shows no 2025–26 change. Source: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/101/II/647. Evidence class GOV.
- **Double damages:** RESOLVED (official host). § 100.20(5) gives "twice the amount of such pecuniary loss, together with costs, including a reasonable attorney fee". Source: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/100/20. Evidence class GOV.
- **2026 law-change sweep:** done by primary-host fetch, not search. Sources read: the 2025 session enacted-acts index (Acts 1–247, https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/2025/related/acts), history lines on every cited section, the DSPS pending-rules page, and the DATCP news-release index. Findings:
  - 2025 Wis. Act 120 (enacted 3/27/2026) creates condition-report item E3m (NID special assessments), effective Oct 1, 2026. Not chimney-related. https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/2025/related/acts/120
  - 2025 Wis. Act 237 (enacted 4/8/2026) amends item F7 (restrictive covenants/deed restrictions). Not chimney-related. https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/2025/related/acts/237
  - 2025 Wis. Act 105 raises the Consumer Act exclusion cap from $25,000 to $50,000, effective 1-1-2027. This widens the 3-day cancel's reach and is now in §4.
  - DSPS "SPS 320 to 325: Update to the Uniform Dwelling Code" is in Drafting Rule status. Nothing adopted. https://dsps.wi.gov/Pages/RulesStatutes/PendingRules.aspx
  - No 2025–26 amendment to §§ 101.647, 101.654 or 423.202, per their history lines.
  - No act in the 247-act index concerns chimneys, fireplaces, or contractor licensing.
  - DATCP July 31, 2026 storm-repair release: general door-to-door caution only; no chimney item. https://datcp.wi.gov/Pages/News_Media/20260731FollowingStormDamageWisconsinConsumersShouldBeCautiousWhenSeekingRepairs.aspx
  - Evidence class GOV.
- **Mirror spot-check (Job 2):** confirmed on official host. The licensing threshold (§ 101.654), seller disclosure (§ 709.03 B5) and CO law (§ 101.647) were all re-read on docs.legis.wisconsin.gov and match. The only differences were corrections the mirrors didn't cause: bond amount and cancel cite.
- **Dead links:** none dead. dsps.wi.gov UDC and Dwelling Contractor pages resolve, as do docs.legis ATCP 110 and all four law.justia.com links from the Sep 15 pass. The Justia links are mirrors and are superseded by the official docs.legis URLs above; do not use them in page copy. New lookup URL license.wi.gov is linked from the DSPS Dwelling Contractor page as the "LicensE Portal". It is a script-rendered app, so its search page could not be machine-read. Confirm it by hand before publishing it as the lookup link.
- **Corrections made this pass:**
  - 3-day cancel: ATCP 110.07 → Wis. Stat. § 423.202 (+ ATCP 110.08, ATCP 127.74(4)), with scope cap and emergency waiver.
  - Bond: $25,000 → not less than $5,000 (restricted certificate under $25,000).
  - DCQ: "12 hours + test" → 12-hour course (no exam in rule text).
  - Permit copy softened to "check locally".
  - Row lookup → license.wi.gov.
- **Template-leakage sweep:** clean. "Illinois" appears only as a labeled comparison in The story, and no other-state statute strings appear.
- **Still open (non-blocking):** DATCP/AG chimney-sweep enforcement actions (pattern-only §8); per-job permit triggers are local.

1. §8 scam section is pattern-only.
2. Chimney-job permit triggers must be framed as "check with your local building inspector".
3. The 3-day cancel must carry the ≤ $25,000 scope ($50,000 from 1-1-2027) and the emergency-waiver warning.
4. Pre-1980 / local-permit interplay with § 101.654 is not asserted.

sections.rawHeading: 1 · Licensing (GOV — high confidence; re-read on official host Sep 25, 2026)
sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; re-read on official host Sep 25, 2026
sections.markdown: Wisconsin credentials **permit-pullers on 1–2 family dwellings, not chimney contractors.** Under **Wis. Stat. § 101.654(1)(a)**, "no person may obtain a building permit unless the person annually obtains from the department a certificate of financial responsibility," completes continuing education, and furnishes proof to the permit issuer. The implementing rule, **Wis. Admin. Code § SPS 305.31(1)**, states it as: "no person may obtain a building permit for a one- or 2-family dwelling unless" the person holds a **Dwelling Contractor** (or **Dwelling Contractor — restricted**) certification **and** holds or employs a certified **Dwelling Contractor Qualifier (DCQ)**. **§ 101.654(1)(b) exempts an owner who resides (or will reside) in the dwelling and applies for a permit to work on it.** Neither text limits the rule to new construction: **any building permit for a one- or two-family dwelling** triggers it — so if a chimney rebuild, reline, or stove install on a house needs a building permit, the contractor pulling that permit must be certified (whether a given chimney job needs a permit is a UDC/local question — see §5). **Financial responsibility (§ 101.654(2)–(2m)):** a surety bond of **not less than $5,000** or general liability insurance of **at least $250,000 per occurrence**, plus worker's-comp and unemployment-insurance compliance; a contractor using a bond under $25,000 gets a **restricted** certificate and may not take work whose estimated cost exceeds the bond. **DCQ (SPS 305.315):** at least **12 hours** in an approved dwelling-construction course within a year before applying, and 12 hours of continuing education per renewal; the rule text shows no state exam. Work that needs no permit — sweeping and most repairs — needs **no state credential at all**; **Wisconsin has no home-improvement or chimney license**, only consumer rules (ATCP 110, ATCP 127, Wis. Stat. ch. 423). Lookup: DSPS LicensE portal / credential search (license.wi.gov).

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: The Dwelling Contractor credential is about financial responsibility and code accountability — **nothing chimney-specific** — and chimney sweeping/non-permit repair needs no credential. Individual certs (CSIA CCS, C-DET; NCSG CCP/CCR) are the only competence signal.

sections.rawHeading: 3 · Home sale (GOV — high confidence; form item read verbatim from the official statute PDF Sep 25, 2026)
sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; form item read verbatim from the official statute PDF Sep 25, 2026
sections.markdown: **Real Estate Condition Report, Wis. Stat. §§ 709.01–.03**: sellers of property with 1–4 dwelling units (with stated exceptions, e.g., never-occupied fiduciaries and transfer-fee-exempt transfers) must furnish a completed statutory report **within 10 days after acceptance** of the contract; a buyer who does not receive it may rescind within **2 business days** after that 10-day period (§ 709.02(1)). The statutory form's **item B5** asks: "Are you aware of defects in a woodburning stove or fireplace or of other defects caused by a fire in a stove or fireplace or elsewhere on the property?" and lists as examples "defects in the chimney, fireplace flue, inserts, or other installed fireplace equipment; or woodburning stoves not installed pursuant to applicable code." **Item B6** asks about defects related to smoke or carbon monoxide detectors or violations of smoke/CO-detector laws. The report is "not a warranty"; "aware" means the owner has notice or knowledge. No inspection is mandated at transfer; NFPA 211 Level 2 stays a NATIONAL STANDARD. *(2025–26 changes to the form — none to B5/B6: 2025 Wis. Act 120 adds item E3m on neighborhood-improvement-district special assessments, effective Oct 1, 2026; 2025 Wis. Act 237 amends item F7 on restrictive covenants/deed restrictions.)*

sections.rawHeading: 4 · Consumer remedies (GOV — high confidence; re-read on official host Sep 25, 2026)
sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; re-read on official host Sep 25, 2026
sections.markdown: **Home Improvement Practices, ATCP 110** (DATCP) sets home improvement contract requirements (ATCP 110.05). **ATCP 110.07 ("Contract cancellation; return of payments") is NOT a cooling-off rule** — it lets a buyer who prepaid cancel and demand a refund when the seller misses a performance deadline or fails to give required delay notice. **The 3-day cancel is in the Wisconsin Consumer Act: Wis. Stat. § 423.202(1)** gives a customer the right to cancel a **"consumer approval transaction" until midnight of the 3rd business day after the merchant gives the § 423.203 notice**. Under **§ 423.201**, that covers a consumer transaction initiated by face-to-face solicitation away from the merchant's regular place of business (or by mail/phone solicitation directed to the customer), consummated away from that place of business, on credit or for cash over $25. Cancellation notice goes by mail and "need not take a particular form." **Emergency waiver (§ 423.202(4)):** the customer may not cancel if they determined a 3-business-day delay would jeopardize health/safety or endanger property **and** gave the merchant a separate signed, dated personal statement — a door-knock "your chimney is dangerous" pitch is exactly where a customer can be pushed to sign one. **ATCP 110.08** requires a home improvement contract that is a consumer approval transaction to comply with ch. 423, and **ATCP 127.74(4)** makes it a prohibited face-to-face practice to fail to give the § 423.203 notice or honor the cancellation. **Scope limit:** the Consumer Act does not apply to consumer transactions with a cash price over **$25,000 — rising to $50,000 on Jan 1, 2027 (2025 Wis. Act 105)** — or to transactions secured by a first-lien real estate mortgage (§ 421.202(6)–(7)). **Damages:** ATCP 110 is adopted under **Wis. Stat. § 100.20(2)** (per its chapter note), and **§ 100.20(5)** gives any person suffering pecuniary loss from a violation **twice the amount of the pecuniary loss, plus costs including a reasonable attorney fee**. Complaints: DATCP + AG.

sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.markdown: Wisconsin runs a **statewide Uniform Dwelling Code (UDC), SPS 320–325** — per DSPS, "the statewide building code for one- and two-family dwellings built since June 1, 1980," enforced in all municipalities. It is Wisconsin's own administrative code (not a straight IRC adoption; DSPS notes its energy chapter was updated to the 2009 IECC effective Jan 1, 2016). Scope per **SPS 320.02–320.04**: the code covers dwellings built on or after its effective dates (SPS 322 Dec 1, 1978; SPS 320, 321, 323–325 June 1, 1980), and **additions and alterations to UDC dwellings must comply with the code "at the time of permit application or the beginning of the project, if no permit is required"** (SPS 320.04(2)). **Key limit for chimney content: homes built before the UDC effective dates sit outside UDC scope** — a municipality may, by ordinance, apply the UDC to additions/alterations of existing dwellings or require permits for work outside the code (SPS 320.02(2)(c)–(d)), so permit rules for older homes are local. Which chimney jobs on a UDC home need a permit is not stated item-by-item in the text read — **treat relines, rebuilds, and solid-fuel appliance installs as "check with your local building inspector," not as a state-wide permit rule**; routine sweeps are maintenance. A DSPS rulemaking to update SPS 320–325 is in "Drafting Rule" status (DSPS pending-rules page, Sep 2026) — nothing adopted yet.

sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.markdown: **Wis. Stat. § 101.647** (re-read on docs.legis.wisconsin.gov Sep 25, 2026; history 2009 a. 158; 2015 a. 55; 2017 a. 330 — no 2025–26 amendment) requires the owner of a dwelling (the duty does not apply to a dwelling with no attached garage, no fireplace, and no fuel-burning appliance; tourist rooming houses excluded) to install a functional CO detector **"in the basement of the dwelling and on each floor level except the attic, garage, or storage area"**; buildings permitted after Feb 1, 2011 with utility service need electrically powered detectors with battery backup; owners must respond within 5 days to written notice of a non-functional detector, and occupants must maintain detectors in their units. Broad standing coverage; **no statewide pre-sale certificate** found. A permitted chimney job is the natural moment to verify alarms.

sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.markdown: No statewide burn-ban regime; outdoor wood boilers regulated locally in many towns. **Northern Wisconsin has among the highest wood-heat density in the country** — a core market.

sections.title: Scam patterns and enforcement
sections.markdown: DATCP and the AG pursue home-improvement fraud under ATCP 110 / § 100.20; the door-knock "we noticed your chimney" pitch is a textbook solicited-contract scenario. **Specific WI chimney-sweep enforcement actions: NOT CONFIRMED** — patterns, not names.

sections.title: Season calendar
sections.markdown: Cold statewide, severe in the north. Burn season ~Oct–Apr (longer up north). Rush: SEP–NOV. Best booking: APR–JUN.

sections.markdown: WI labor near or slightly below national; Milwaukee/Madison metros near national. Use national ranges until listings data.

story.heading: The story
story.markdown: Wisconsin credentials the people who **pull permits** on your house, not the ones who **clean and repair the chimney** — the Dwelling Contractor certificate is about financial responsibility and code accountability, and sweeping or non-permit repair sits entirely outside it. The state pairs that gap with real protections: a **uniform statewide dwelling code** (for homes built since mid-1980), **double damages for home-improvement rule violations**, and a **seller condition report that names the fireplace and woodstove.** It lands in the same family as Illinois (comparison) — no chimney license, but a disclosure that actually discloses — in one of the highest wood-heat markets in the country.

h1: Wisconsin chimney & fireplace laws: know your rights
metaDescription: Wisconsin chimney & fireplace laws: licensing, seller disclosure, right to cancel and CO alarm rules, with statutes cited.

season.note: Cold statewide, severe in the north. Burn season ~Oct–Apr (longer up north). Rush: SEP–NOV. Best booking: APR–JUN.

faq.q: What should I check before hiring a chimney company in Wisconsin?
faq.a: State licensing: Dwelling Contractor cert required to obtain any 1–2 family dwelling building permit (Wis. Stat. 101.654; SPS 305.31; owner-occupants exempt); NO home-improvement/chimney license. Registration or credential: cert regime ($5k+ bond or $250k liability insurance) + ATCP 110 duties. Seller disclosure at sale: YES — § 709.02–.03 Real Estate Condition Report. Right to cancel a sale made at your home: YES — Wis. Stat. § 423.202 for consumer approval (home-solicited) transactions ≤ $25,000 cash price ($50,000 from 1-1-2027); emergency waiver § 423.202(4). Carbon monoxide alarm law: broad (§ 101.647, basement + every floor). Where to check a contractor: DSPS LicensE credential search (license.wi.gov). Then ask the eight questions below, get the inspection findings in writing with photos, and never sign for "emergency" work on the day of a door-knock.

faq.q: Is a chimney inspection required when a home sells in Wisconsin?
faq.a: Real Estate Condition Report, Wis. Stat. §§ 709.01–.03: sellers of property with 1–4 dwelling units (with stated exceptions, e.g., never-occupied fiduciaries and transfer-fee-exempt transfers) must furnish a completed statutory report within 10 days after acceptance of the contract; a buyer who does not receive it may rescind within 2 business days after that 10-day period (§ 709.02(1)). The statutory form's item B5 asks: "Are you aware of defects in a woodburning stove or fireplace or of other defects caused by a fire in a stove or fireplace or elsewhere on the property?" and lists as examples "defects in the chimney, fireplace flue, inserts, or other installed fireplace equipment; or woodburning stoves not installed pursuant to applicable code." Item B6 asks about defects related to smoke or carbon monoxide detectors or violations of smoke/CO-detector laws.

faq.q: Can I cancel a chimney contract I signed at my door in Wisconsin?
faq.a: Home Improvement Practices, ATCP 110 (DATCP) sets home improvement contract requirements (ATCP 110.05). ATCP 110.07 ("Contract cancellation; return of payments") is NOT a cooling-off rule — it lets a buyer who prepaid cancel and demand a refund when the seller misses a performance deadline or fails to give required delay notice. The 3-day cancel is in the Wisconsin Consumer Act: Wis. Stat.
